e-5466.knowledge_point: Calculating a Vector Given Its Image Under a Linear Transformation
e-5466.problem:
The vector $\mathbf{v}$ in the plane is mapped to the vector $[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 4\end{aligned}]$ under the action of the linear transformation $\mathbf{T}$ whose matrix $T$ is given by

$$
[\begin{aligned}5 & -2 \\ 10 & -3\end{aligned}]
$$

What is the original vector $\mathbf{v}?$
e-5466.worked_solution:
From the given information, we have

$$
[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 4\end{aligned}]
$$

We need to reverse the action of the matrix $T.$ So, we multiply the above equation by $T^{-1},$ and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{-1}\cdot T\cdot v & ={T}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 \\ 4\end{aligned}] \\ v & ={T}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 \\ 4\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we need to calculate the inverse of $T$, which is

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{-1} & =\frac{1}{-15-(-20)}[\begin{aligned}-3 & 2 \\ -10 & 5\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{5}[\begin{aligned}-3 & 2 \\ -10 & 5\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the original vector is

$$
\begin{aligned}v & ={T}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 \\ 4\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{5}[\begin{aligned}-3 & 2 \\ -10 & 5\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 \\ 4\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{5}[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 10\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

e-5467.knowledge_point: Calculating the Vertices of a Polygon Given Its Image Under a Linear Transformation
e-5467.problem:
Consider the linear transformation $\mathbf T$ with matrix representation $T,$ given by

$$
[\begin{aligned}4 & -1 \\ 3 & 1\end{aligned}]
$$

The triangle $S$ is mapped to the triangle $S'$ under the action of $\mathbf T.$ The triangle $S'$ has vertices $(4,3),(4,10),$ and $(-4,-3).$ Which of the following are vertices of $S?$

- $(1,0)$

- $(4,-3)$

- $(-1,0)$
e-5467.worked_solution:
First, we create a matrix $Y$ containing all of the vertices of $S'\mathbin{:}$ 

$$
[\begin{aligned}4 & 4 & -4 \\ 3 & 10 & -3\end{aligned}]
$$

Now, if $X$ denotes the matrix that contains the corresponding vertices of $S$, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}T\cdot X & =Y \\ T\cdot X & =[\begin{aligned}4 & 4 & -4 \\ 3 & 10 & -3\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

We need to reverse the action of the matrix $T.$ So, we multiply the above equation by $T^{-1},$ and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{-1}\cdot T\cdot X & ={T}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}4 & 4 & -4 \\ 3 & 10 & -3\end{aligned}] \\ X & ={T}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}4 & 4 & -4 \\ 3 & 10 & -3\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The inverse of $T$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{-1} & =\frac{1}{4-(-3)}[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ -3 & 4\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{7}[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ -3 & 4\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}X & ={T}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}4 & 4 & -4 \\ 3 & 10 & -3\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{7}[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ -3 & 4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}4 & 4 & -4 \\ 3 & 10 & -3\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{7}[\begin{aligned}7 & 14 & -7 \\ 0 & 28 & 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -1 \\ 0 & 4 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

As a result, the coordinates of the vertices of the original triangle are $(1,0),(2,4),(-1,0).$

Therefore, the correct answer is "I and III only."

decision.explanation: The determinant of T is 10, so T^{-1}=\frac{1}{10}\begin{bmatrix}2&-4\\2&1\end{bmatrix}. Thus v=T^{-1}\begin{bmatrix}-2\\-3\end{bmatrix}=\frac{1}{10}\begin{bmatrix}8\\-7\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}4/5\\-7/10\end{bmatrix}, which is option d.

after.name: Question 1
after.problem:
The vector $v$ in the plane is mapped to the vector $[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ -3\end{aligned}]$ under the action of the linear transformation $T$ whose matrix $T$ is given by

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}1 & 4 \\ -2 & 2\end{aligned}].
$$

What is the original vector $v?$
after.worked_solution:
From the given information, we have 

$$
T\cdot v=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ -3\end{aligned}].
$$

We need to reverse the action of the matrix $T.$ So, we multiply the above equation by ${T}^{-1},$ and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{-1}\cdot T\cdot v & ={T}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}-2 \\ -3\end{aligned}] \\ v & ={T}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}-2 \\ -3\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we need to calculate the inverse of $T$, which is

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{-1} & =\frac{1}{2-(-8)}[\begin{aligned}2 & -4 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{10}[\begin{aligned}2 & -4 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the original vector is

$$
\begin{aligned}v & ={T}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}-2 \\ -3\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{10}[\begin{aligned}2 & -4 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-2 \\ -3\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{10}[\begin{aligned}8 \\ -7\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{4}{5} \\ -\frac{7}{10}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

content.problem:
The vector $v$ in the plane is mapped to the vector $[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ -3\end{aligned}]$ under the action of the linear transformation $T$ whose matrix $T$ is given by

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}1 & 4 \\ -2 & 2\end{aligned}].
$$

What is the original vector $v?$
content.worked_solution:
From the given information, we have 

$$
T\cdot v=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ -3\end{aligned}].
$$

We need to reverse the action of the matrix $T.$ So, we multiply the above equation by ${T}^{-1},$ and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{-1}\cdot T\cdot v & ={T}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}-2 \\ -3\end{aligned}] \\ v & ={T}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}-2 \\ -3\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we need to calculate the inverse of $T$, which is

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{-1} & =\frac{1}{2-(-8)}[\begin{aligned}2 & -4 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{10}[\begin{aligned}2 & -4 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the original vector is

$$
\begin{aligned}v & ={T}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}-2 \\ -3\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{10}[\begin{aligned}2 & -4 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-2 \\ -3\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{10}[\begin{aligned}8 \\ -7\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{4}{5} \\ -\frac{7}{10}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

content.problem:
The vector $v$ in the plane is mapped to the vector $[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -2\end{aligned}]$ under the action of the linear transformation $T$ whose matrix $T$ is given by

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}2 & 5 \\ 1 & 3\end{aligned}].
$$

What is the original vector $v?$
content.worked_solution:
From the given information, we have 

$$
T\cdot v=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -2\end{aligned}].
$$

We need to reverse the action of the matrix $T.$ So, we multiply the above equation by ${T}^{-1},$ and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{-1}\cdot T\cdot v & ={T}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 \\ -2\end{aligned}] \\ v & ={T}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 \\ -2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we need to calculate the inverse of $T$, which is

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{-1} & =\frac{1}{6-5}[\begin{aligned}3 & -5 \\ -1 & 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 & -5 \\ -1 & 2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the original vector is

$$
\begin{aligned}v & ={T}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 \\ -2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 & -5 \\ -1 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 \\ -2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}13 \\ -5\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$
